game: D.C.P.S. - Da Capo 1 Plus Situation Portable (PSP, NPJH50731)
source: D.C.P.S. ID Translation (Custom 0 lines + EN Fallback)

messages.210: My mind roared, as I flew out of the house.
messages.255:
Chasing Nemu and on the verge of lateness, I dashed on the
path to school.
messages.311:
Slanting in one direction at an intersection while passing a
bicycle, I turned the corner to the shortest route.
messages.412: This will have to be non-stop action all the way there!
messages.500: The sound of a musical instrument could be heard ahead.
messages.539:
Getting a better look, it is a girl wearing the uniform of
the main school, tottering her way towards it.
messages.645:
Slowing my pace to make sure I don't frighten her, I ease
past her from her side.
messages.711: As I passed her by, I took a casual glance to my side--
messages.781:
The girl was walking with her eyes closed, all the while
playing a small xylophone rhythmically.
messages.896:
I unconciously turned my head backwards, staring at the girl
with thoughts transfixed, as my speed fell dramatically.
messages.1052:
I finally ran through the door to class, creeping to my desk
and trying to settle down.
messages.1161: I looked upwards at the classroom's clock.
messages.1259:
For some reason, there's still 5 minutes before the bell
rings...
messages.1362: Nemu approached with a calm smile.
messages.1472:
"The early bird gets the worm. From now on, you really
should wake up early."
messages.1791:
"You just about got here 5 minutes early with your top
speed. That's pretty good!"
messages.1990:
"W, when I left the house... Haah... I didn't think I could
make it..."
messages.2183:
"Did you remember to fix your clock? The one that's set 5
minutes in advance?"
messages.2373: With a sweet smile, Nemu returned to her desk.
messages.2561: "I sincerely believe in Amitabha, Lord have mercy on me."
messages.2651: Receiving this crap all the time, it's almost unbearable.
messages.2698:
That Suginami, even though he acts so casual all the time,
he's actually has the top marks of the class, a blip in
society.
messages.2792: Even worse, he's good at pretty much all sports.
messages.2881:
"By the way Asakura, I've come up with a magnificent
project. You'd participate in it, of course?"
messages.2955: "Wouldn't it be more like a stupid project?"
messages.3002:
Whenever it's from this guy, it always seems like that's the
case.
messages.3075:
"Of course not. It's a quiz competition based on the
question "How many people will confess to Shirakawa Kotori
before graduation?""
messages.3259:
"Not at all! Just look at the list of people who've already
signed up. The person with the correct answer is given a big
prize."
messages.3391:
"Right now, the most popular range is around the 50-60
mark."
messages.3510:
"Nah, it's Shirakawa Kotori after all. I'm going for a dark
horse bet, I think 100 people will confess to her by then."
messages.3638:
Even for that crazy amount of people, knowing her
popularity, I wouldn't say it's impossible...
messages.3807:
Looking up behind me, it's my classmate, Mizukoshi Mako,
glaring at us with scornful eyes.
messages.3921: "I'm not with him, Mako. I'm an honest man."
messages.4016:
"What are you saying, comrade Asakura. Are we not
comrades-in-arms, fighting the same battle?"
messages.4162:
"Last week, the arcade center, zombie extermination, using
guns, you and I, to prevent the evil ambitions of the
teachers."
messages.4363: Our palms firmly met each other's.
messages.4558:
As the bell went off, the form teacher Shirakawa Koyomi
arrived at the classroom.
messages.4789:
While dashing to school, a mysterious girl with her eyes
half-closed, rhythmically playing a xylophone, was seen.
messages.4887:
I was a bit worried for her, but I had enough on my plate,
and passed her by without disturbing her trance.
messages.4982:
Reaching the "alternate dimension" school with time to
spare, Nemu told me about her adjustments to my clock...

messages.216: An unsurprising, calm nature to their flight.
messages.256:
Like a flower's petals scattered from an angel's wings, as
if all of eternity was defined in a moment.
messages.386:
While stepping on the piles of snowy cherry blossoms like a
carpet of white frost, I try to take in these thoughts.
messages.464:
"(Jokes aside, a serious nature definitely doesn't suit
me.)"
messages.544:
Looking further into the surroundings, they seem to stretch
on forever in an endless world.
messages.616: Only the cherry trees stand out, swaying silently.
messages.684:
It's rare to see a dream without the person dreaming it
involved.
messages.721:
I dizzily walked in a direction, as if literally in the
middle of a dream.
messages.841:
I'd rather not have a power that makes me seem like a
psychic or warlock, but that's the weird power I posess.
messages.929:
In the real world, someone with such a weird power normally
seen in stories or games, would certainly be thought to be
cool.
messages.1026:
No matter the painful circumstances, just being normal would
be better--
messages.1104: That's what I wish I could shout out to everyone!
messages.1155:
"(Other people's dreams are usually more interesting than
this...)"
messages.1206:
With a sigh, I continue to wander around this peaceful
world.
messages.1307:
Without knowing the origins of the dream, a stranger's dream
is the height of incomprehension.
messages.1401:
If I don't know the person, even seeing a sordid romance or
a risky adventure isn't fun.
messages.1498:
It's like a B-grade movie, with a less interesting script
than usual.
messages.1578:
"(Then again, my appearance here means that this has to be
the dream of someone I know.)"
messages.1646:
Furthermore, since I'm actually here, probably someone close
to me.
messages.1740:
"(There aren't many people around who would have this kind
of poetic dream either...)"
messages.1828:
With a snap of my fingers, I could probably make it tomorrow
for both parties.
messages.1906:
"(Hehehe... you who would disturb my sleep, prepare to feel
my wrath--)"
messages.1994: But as my fingers made contact, there was no sound.
messages.2031:
A giant sakura tree, as if the God guiding the lessers,
materialized.
messages.2151:
As the joke flew out of my mouth, the watcher's mood swung
dramatically.
messages.2231: My eyes feel like they're burning from within.
messages.2250:
My voice lost its power as the tense atmosphere mixed with
the person's mood.
messages.2347: The surreal scene quickly gave me goosebumps.
messages.2390:
The dancing sakura petals scattered to reveal the figure of
a young girl.
messages.2462:
--That girl, with the look of an angel, but the air of a
devil.
messages.2614: "(...Aah, that's right. This is a dream after all.)"
messages.2659: A bitter smile followed those words that came to mind.
messages.2721:
I may have forgotten her name, but I at least remember that
this girl is a childhood friend of mine.
messages.2802: "I can't see you, are you really there?"
messages.2875: "That's right... I can feel you here."
messages.2912:
The thick voice from her heart, like someone who's
unintentionally stepped into the strike zone.
messages.3020:
"If this is a dream... then maybe, when we wake up, we won't
remember anything..."
messages.3096: The girl's sad face tugged at my heartstrings.
messages.3137:
But stretching out my hand, hugging her, or even calling
out, are things I can't do now...
messages.3225:
--Because I'm just a bystander, who can do nothing but watch
this unchangeable dream.--
messages.3409:
The dream after the end of winter, but before the start of
spring.
messages.3452:
The point of time with no significance--Da Capo, the
beginning and ending of the dream.
messages.3706: Whose dream was it? It has to be someone who I know...
messages.3803:
...A small girl, my old childhood friend. With a cloudy
expression, the girl spoke softly.
messages.3942:
The dream after the end of winter, but before the start of
spring.
messages.3985:
The point of time with no significance--Da Capo, the
beginning and ending of the dream.

messages.133:
The morning sun's rays penetrated my eyelids, alerting me
that the time to get up has arrived.
messages.299:
As I open my eyes, for some reason, I see my sister right up
close to my face, peering at me.
messages.415:
I woke up first, so I was just looking at your sleeping
face..."
messages.487:
Displaying the servitude of a million adoring younger
sisters, she replied with a smile.
messages.563:
"That isn't...well, disregarding that, why are you sleeping
here in the first place?
messages.668:
"Why... don't we always sleep together? You're slow today,
onii-chan♪"
messages.760: As she said that, her finger lightly tapped my forehead.
messages.906: "Hey, onii-chan... let's do our usual morning greeting."
messages.962: Nemu closed her eyes slowly with those words.
messages.1037: Yes, it must be. There's no way this could be reality.
messages.1221:
Now that I know this is a dream, there's nothing to be
afraid of!
messages.1270: The meal is laid before me. Now I must gratefully accept it.
messages.1473:
Something hard entered my mouth, signalling the end of the
meal.
messages.1573: "Good morning nii-san. The weather's fantastic today~!"
messages.1620:
...Finally awakening, Nemu stood by my bedside, happily
peering into my face.
messages.1747:
On this morning, the only words that could escape my mouth
was gibberish.
messages.1815: In my mouth, was the unpleasant taste of my bedside clock.
messages.1968:
I spit out the clock, moaning slightly while massaging my
cheeks and chin.
messages.2060: "What was that? You sound like a robot from 20 years ago."
messages.2157: Oh good, my normal voice returned.
messages.2225: A quick salute, and I fell back onto my futon.
messages.2286:
"Geez, if you mess around this much, you're going to be
late!"
messages.2342:
"It's fine. I worked out exactly how much time I need to get
to the classroom from here."
messages.2421: "So you're going to school in your pajamas?!"
messages.2508: I slowly rose from the futon again.
messages.2682: With a final parting shot, she started to leave the room.
messages.2804:
With her hand on the doorknob, she turned her head back
towards me.
messages.2837: "We haven't done the morning routine yet."
messages.2892:
"Ehh, it's, fine... it's okay for today... besides, there's
no time...
messages.2964:
Her arms across her chest, she hastily shook her head no
with her back to the doorway.
messages.3022: "Don't whine so much about it, let's just get it over with."
messages.3110:
Gesturing her over with my finger, Nemu let out a small moan
and slowly returned.
messages.3188:
With her face so close to mine, I can see the red flush in
her cheeks.
messages.3302:
Nemu stood facing the bedside, her hips bending slightly and
her hands on my shoulders.
messages.3370:
As the distance between us rapidly decreased, we could feel
each other's breath.
messages.3481: Close enough to count the creases on her lips.
messages.3533: I put my hand on the back of Nemu's head... and pulled.
messages.3702: I used my forehead to measure the hotness of hers.
messages.3802: "Uu... Why must we always butt heads like this?"
messages.3853: "I have to measure your temperature. You know it's no joke."
messages.3971: Nemu muttered while rubbing her forehead.
messages.4008:
"You've always had a weak constitution, a thermometer
wouldn't be reliable in your case."
messages.4125:
"Besides, if we used a thermometer, would you be able to
take me supervising you through it?"
messages.4215:
"With the top button of your shirt unfastened, putting the
thermometer under your arm?"
messages.4429:
Not the normal morning chatter. At least it's a short break
from the normal school routine, something to be thankful
for.
messages.4537: "Man... anyway, hurry up before it gets any later."
messages.4613: Nemu disappears out the door, her footsteps growing distant.
messages.4713: Should I sleep a bit longer?
messages.4993:
I had a weird dream. I was then rather forcefully
awakened...
messages.5112:
The one who did so was Nemu. To wake me up, she stuffed my
mouth rather roughly.
messages.5180:
After doing the usual morning forehead-to-forehead checkup,
Nemu's figure disappeared beyond the door.

messages.249:
Exchanging "greetings" with a fellow classmate, I sat at my
desk.
messages.313:
Nemu, sitting in the front row, was chatting with her female
friends.
messages.416: I fell prostrate onto my desk.
messages.456:
"Ohh, Asakura. This time you're actually prepared for the
morning."
messages.495:
The grinning Suginami, as always, approached my desk before
the class starts.
messages.561: "Where do you see any preparation here?"
messages.621:
As he got closer, I looked up to the face of one of the best
examples of a worst friend.
messages.811:
Even though he acts so casual all the time, he's actually
has the top marks of the class, a blip in society.
messages.893: Even worse, he's good at pretty much all sports.
messages.962:
"By the way Asakura, I've come up with a magnificent
project. You'd participate in it, of course?"
messages.1036: "Wouldn't it be more like a stupid project?"
messages.1083:
Whenever it's from this guy, it always seems like that's the
case.
messages.1156:
"Of course not. It's a wonderful quiz competition centered
around the question "How many people will confess to
Shirakawa Kotori before her graduation?""
messages.1340:
"What are you talking about! Just look at the list of people
who've already signed up. Naturally, the person with the
correct answer will be awarded a spectacular prize."
messages.1472:
"Right now, the most popular range is around the 50-60
mark."
messages.1591:
"Nah, it's Shirakawa Kotori after all. I'm going for a dark
horse bet, I think 100 people will confess to her by then."
messages.1719:
Even for that crazy amount of people, knowing her
popularity, I wouldn't say it's impossible...
messages.1888:
Looking up behind me, it's my classmate, Mizukoshi Mako,
glaring at us with scornful eyes.
messages.2002: "I'm not with him, Mako. I'm an honest man."
messages.2102:
"What are you saying, comrade Asakura. Are we not
comrades-in-arms, fighting the same battle?"
messages.2248:
"Last week, the arcade center, zombie extermination, using
guns, you and I, to prevent the evil ambitions of the
teachers."
messages.2449: Our palms firmly met each other's.
messages.2629:
As the bell went off, the form teacher Shirakawa Koyomi
arrived at the classroom.
messages.2846:
Upon entering the classroom, as usual, Suginami was nearby
spouting crap.
messages.2934:
Before he could go too far, the chime rang, and Shirakawa
Koyomi-sensei entered the classroom.

messages.275:
Swinging my bag onto my shoulders, I started walking
leisurely.
messages.345:
Facing the potrait of several dancing and scattered sakura
petals, Nemu and I walked down the avenue of trees in a
line.
messages.507:
"See, when was the last time you were able to walk so
lesiurely to school?"
messages.567: Nemu skipped ahead and turned her head back to me.
messages.721:
"A hasty, hot-tempered one wouldn't be of much use, would
it?"
messages.777:
"That isn't a problem of hastiness, it's one of your own
prerogative."
messages.833: A lecture by the honour student.
messages.969:
Pretending to ignore the reprimand。 I began to study the
dancing sakura petals.
messages.1049:
As the light winds slowly die out, the sakura petals float
their last and fall to the ground.
messages.1176:
"These petals, blooming again after just a year... it's
weird."
messages.1242:
Although I accepted this as fact when I was just a kid, in
the end, it's still strange,
messages.1371: "I like it that way. They're pretty."
messages.1406:
"I wonder if you'd think that way when you have to sweep
them up."
messages.1498:
In order to clean up all that "emotion", requires a rather
large amount of work and money...
messages.1570:
Walking through the thick-lying sakura petals, we continue
towards the school.
messages.1848: As always, Nemu and I head for school together.

messages.269: The usual starting of the school day.
messages.300:
Normal school, normal classroom, normal homeroom. That is,
except for one thing...
messages.402: "Class, we'd be having a new student from today onwards."
messages.449: An exchange student? It's an odd time to take one in...
messages.486:
The formerly quiet classroom burst into murmurs. All eyes,
filled with curiosity, concentrated on the front of the
class.
messages.562: The "new classmate" stood by the teacher's desk.
messages.640:
The girl standing there seemed to be quite old-fashioned and
quiet. A pretty girl, as well.
messages.716:
This will increase the girls ratio of this class. With the
amount of useless guys here, that has to be a good thing.
messages.803:
"She was supposed to go to the main school, but there were
some complications at the time."
messages.861:
"For the convenience of her Shinto Shrine family, she has
been attached to this class."
messages.973: "My name is Konomiya Tamaki. I am pleased to meet everyone."
messages.1047:
With a respectful bow, the Shinto daughter introduced
herself.
messages.1151:
Straightening her uniform, she emits a kind of peaceful aura
around her.
messages.1207:
With my fingers on my chin, I observe the still-standing
Konomiya Tamaki.
messages.1269: Mm, cute... And seems to have a refined upbringing as well.
messages.1358:
After introducing herself, the exchange student started
looking left and right of the classroom, as if looking for
someone.
messages.1555:
Koyomi looked in my direction. Following her, Tamaki was
soon looking at me as well.
messages.1684: The exchange student Konomiya stared fervently at me.
messages.1725:
I don't think I've seen this girl before. Why would she know
my name?
messages.1805:
Don't tell me it's a long-lost sister, seperated at birth,
finally re-united again.
messages.1859: Or maybe, a hitman targeting me?
messages.1939:
Konomiya's eyes' death grip on me would not waver. Along
with that, the rest of the class was soon staring at me as
well.
messages.2208: The shock ran right through the classroom.
messages.2237:
The entire class was soon stirring with murmured
exclamations.
messages.2285: Eh? What did she just say?
messages.2333: Fiancee as in, the person you promise to marry?
messages.2424: Argh, who the heck is she???
messages.2457: I made a full search of the hard disk in my brain.
messages.2502: I had done such a wonderful thing in my life?
messages.2711: "Oh, so that's how you know him."
messages.2750:
"W, Wait a minute teacher! What's with that comment! I've
never met this girl before!"
messages.2863:
Koyomi-sensei... she took that so easily. Why wasn't she
baffled at all!
messages.2933:
It should be more like "That's crazy!" or "Isn't that a bit
too fast?"....right?
messages.3035:
"Is that so. Then, whatever Asakura doesn't know, please
explain to him."
messages.3205: Tamaki also, replying in the same fashion...
messages.3252: As if she's really my fiancee...
messages.3369:
"...No, really, I don't know what this girl is talking
about!"
messages.3475:
Desperately looking for someone to back me up, I glance in
Nemu's direction.
messages.3554: Meeting my eyes with hers, Nemu smiled sweetly at me.
messages.3599:
Come on... you don't realize this is all a misunderstanding?
That smile is scary...
messages.3696:
The class, still reeling from the shock of the fiancee
announcement, were whispering back and forth.
messages.3803:
"Alright, everyone settle down. We can confirm the details
during the break."
messages.3898:
"I'll begin today's class. Konomiya, please go to your
seat."
messages.3984:
As if reprimanded, she walked to her seat with her head
down.
messages.4064: And as she reached my desk, her footsteps stopped.
messages.4184: "Uh, about you being my fiancee and all..."
messages.4251: "From here on... let us get along well."
messages.4375: In the end, cowed by Konomiya's smile, I returned her words.
messages.4466:
Konomiya smiled once more, then respectfully bowed again and
left for her seat at the rear of the classroom.
messages.4623: I can't wait for the break period.
messages.4650: Today's lesson seems even longer than usual...
messages.4699: Of course, it's all the fault of that fiancee declaration.
messages.4744: Frankly, the current lesson is nothing compared to that.
messages.4789:
Why does this exchange student, whom I've never met before,
know who I am?
messages.4853: Maybe we met in a previous life...
messages.4892: ...I quickly shed such fairlytale thoughts out of my head.
messages.4937: The truth must be that I have amnesia...
messages.5086: "Oh, if it isn't Nemu! How are you doing?"
messages.5131:
With a huge (and forced) smile, I energetically waved my
hand.
messages.5223: "Don't try to hide things with fake cheerfulness!"
messages.5400: "You know what I'm talking about, don't you?"
messages.5451: "...The menu for this evening's dinner, right?"
messages.5526:
"Instead of talking here, shall we go to the cafeteria
instead?"
messages.5590:
"...Oh, so you want to talk about something so embarassing
no one else can hear!"
messages.5688:
"If you don't stop fooling around, we're going back home
instead."
messages.5813:
My mental state now is that of a kid trying to run away from
a scolding.
messages.5879: Urgh... I want to be somewhere far away right now.
messages.5924:
Knowing my modest wish was not goint to be granted, I
accompany Nemu to the cafeteria.
messages.6033: Time to prepare myself... the accused.
messages.6099: "Nii-san, shall we continue where we left off?"
messages.6138: In front of me, was reverse-mode Nemu.
messages.6167: Her face was smiling, hiding her obvious mood.
messages.6210: In front of me was a bowl of udon.
messages.6233: Nemu had a bowl of oyakudon.
messages.6258:
However, her food had not even been touched. Nemu's mouth
was being used right now for interrogation purposes.
messages.6367: "Hurry up and eat before your food gets cold."
messages.6400:
Trying to keep my heartbeat and mental state normal, I slurp
down my noodles.
messages.6514:
"Geez! Stop playing your deception games already! Of course
I'm talking about the whole fiancee business!"
messages.6580: With those words, she took my chopsticks away.
messages.6646:
"D, don't act like that! I really didn't know about the
fiancee thing. Absolutely nothing about it!"
messages.6785:
"I'm not lying! Today was really the first day I ever met
Konomiya."
messages.6899:
"Then why did this entire thing come about in the first
place? Please explain precisely!"
messages.6981: "Did you listen to what I said at all?"
messages.7014:
Grabbing back my chopsticks from her, I quickly resumed my
lunch.
messages.7097:
"Geez! I've been with you for so long, and this is really
the first time I've heard of this!"
messages.7371: "The main subject of the gossip....is here."
messages.7409: I motioned with my head to the entrance of the cafeteria.
messages.7452: Nemu slowly turned towards the direction I indicated.
messages.7515:
Standing at the entrance, Konomiya slowly entered the
cafeteria.
messages.7642: Konomiya restlessly looked around the entire cafeteria.
messages.7752:
Konomiya had her hand on her uniform, and abruptly threw
them off her.
messages.7890:
Time stopped as the uniform hung in midair. Below the flung
uniform, a pure white robe and hakama materialized from
nowhere.
messages.7999: I spontaneously spat out the udon I was eating.
messages.8090: "That, that has to be, a Shinto shrine..."
messages.8180:
As Konomiya straightened her spine, I tried to figure how
what she's trying to do, and failed horribly...
messages.8250:
All I knew was, a shrine maiden is in Kazami Academy's
cafeteria right now.
messages.8301: "It was said that her family are Shinto..."
messages.8361: "But that has nothing to do with this situation!"
messages.8425:
"Nemu, how on earth did she managed to fit that bulky
costume under her uniform?"
messages.8537:
The idle sibling conversation certainly did not match what
was happening right now...
messages.8599:
Konomiya, again producing something from nothing, suddenly
had a bow and arrow in her hands.
messages.8678: "Wha, a, a bow?! Does she think she'a an archer?!"
messages.8831:
Konomiya slowly pulled back on the bow's string, and then
her hand released it.
messages.8885: My eyes instinctively followed the route of the arrow.
messages.8969:
The arrow had pierced the bowl of a poor male student near
us, splitting it into two equal pieces.
messages.9080: But there aren't any cameras around...
messages.9148: All eyes in the cafeteria immediately centered on Konomiya.
messages.9183:
Konomiya remained still, holding her bow and arrow and in
her shrine maiden costume like some sort of fighting game
character.
messages.9306:
The poor male student, with his bowl split in half,
absentmindedly gazed at her.
messages.9409:
"My deepest apologies. I was overstepping my bounadries... I
am deeply sorry for scaring you."
messages.9497: With those words, Konomiya deeply bowed to the guy.
messages.9608: "...Do you think she was aiming for me, brother?"
messages.9678:
"Don't worry, I bet everyone else in this classroom is
asking the same question."
messages.9792:
"...I don't know. First time I've ever seen, or heard of
something like this."
messages.9884: Konomiya approached us, and started talking to us.
messages.10079:
"Wh, what's wrong Nemu? You, your voice seems to have gotten
higher?"
messages.10179:
Whether she noticed our obvious nervousness, Konomiya
remained cool and calm.
messages.10300: "I am very sorry for just now."
messages.10375:
"In class... I did not think that I would shock so many
people."
messages.10469: "My parents had decided that I was to be your fiancee."
messages.10523: "So I thought that I should bring it up..."
messages.10613: In that moment, all my fears dropped out of my head.
messages.10690: "I am really sorry for being such a bother."
messages.10723:
And as she smiled and apologized at the same time, her face
showed no signs of worry about the situation she just
described.
messages.10791: If that's the case, then I have nothing to fear either.
messages.10830: At least, now I can find out exactly what's going on.
messages.10912:
"You say your parents decided that you were to be my
fiancee? I'm certain that I've never met your parents
though, have I?"

messages.11811:
"Well, it's not really acquainted in my case... today was
more or less the first time we met."
messages.11885:
Even with my halfhearted denial, Seiba-san continued smiling
happily.
messages.11956:
After a bit more idle conversation with Seiba-san, Miharu
and I left the Tsukishiro mansion.
messages.12109:
"That mansion was really huge! The first time I've ever been
in a house like that."
messages.12183: "Not to mention having a butler and other servants..."
messages.12293: "I bet there isn't a single manga in that house."
messages.12361: "Ha, she's more likely to read Poe and Sebastian."
messages.12492: Miharu and I nodded in agreement.
messages.12531: "But anyway, that girl... she's still very mysterious."
messages.12615: "She must be lonely all the time..."
messages.12689:
the big and mysterious-coloured eyes came flooding back into
my memory.
messages.12747:
Empty eyes which seemed to be staring far away at
nothingness.
messages.12796:
She looked transparent and delicate, as if crafted out of
glass. It felt like touching her would make her break into
pieces.
messages.12993:
With the memory of the girl standing in the deserted area of
the back of the gym still in my head, I muttered my
approval.
messages.13222:
I went back to school on a Sunday to retrieve something I
forgot to.
messages.13265:
Because the graduation party was coming soon, there were
lots of students still in the school. Feeling a bit shameful
in my casual clothes, I decide to try to sneak my way out
using the backdoor of the gymnasium.
messages.13380:
At the back of the gymnasium was a lone girl. She looked as
fragile as transparent glass.
messages.13458:
She was staring at a plant growing in front of her. Instead
of replying to my attempts to talk to her, she used a doll
she held close to her chest to answer my questions.
messages.13589:
With such a weird atmosphere, the girl quickly cut the
conversation off, and after the girl (or rather, the doll)
warned to be careful around the plant, ran off somewhere.
messages.13722:
In her rush, the girl dropped her student notebook, which I
retrieved off the floor.
messages.13796:
I met Miharu en-route to her house, and we returned the
student notebook together.
messages.13882:
We could somehow feel that this girl was lonely, and decided
to try and befriend her.

messages.177:
Unsurprisingly, there isn't many people in school on a
Sunday. I could hear the faint voices of the exercise club
in the distance.
messages.269:
The Feburary weather is cold. Couple that with the school
not switching on the heaters on Sunday... no wonder that I'm
shivering.
messages.372: My footsteps resounded down the empty corridor as I walked.
messages.436: "Haa... why did I come here in the first place?"
messages.514:
I turned my head to the sound of the voice behind me.
Standing there was a smiling male, whose name was alien to
me.
messages.786: "Since when did you become my emperor, huh."
messages.903:
"Anyway, what are you doing here? In your school uniform, no
less."
messages.1057:
"And my school uniform makes me that much more stealthy
while performing my work."
messages.1168: "If that explains enough, I'd return to my duty."
messages.1229:
The omega idiot, carrying a strangely bulging bag, quickly
disappeared into the teacher's room.
messages.1299: There aren't any lessons now, so what the hell is he doing?
messages.1359: "I shouldn't think too much about this."
messages.1390:
Forgetting about Suginami's affairs, I continue wandering
the school grounds.
messages.1516:
I already spend six days a week staring at the school's
interior, why did I come here for the seventh again?
messages.1624: I stop at the entrance to the music room.
messages.1657: I can hear faint voices coming from inside.
messages.1696: I place my ear on the door and silence my breathing.
messages.1742: The only thing that graces my ears is a deathly silence.
messages.1765:
I suppose it's a fair problem if any sound could escape from
a music room.
messages.1833: "...I bet I look pretty suspicious too."
messages.1905:
But I didn't feel like stopping. Besides, on a rest day at
school, there's not much else to do, and no one to see me
anyway.
messages.2049: Looks like no one's in there--
messages.2093: "No, wrong! That's not how it's supposed to be, geez!"
messages.2161: Well... guess there are people inside...
messages.2208: "...And why does that voice sound so familiar?"
messages.2270: I unconciously put my hand on the doorknob.
messages.2366: The truth was that I do know the owner of that voice.
messages.2401:
It looked like a music club practice session-- except there
were only two people inside.
messages.2459:
Inside, Moe-senpai and Mako were happily playing their
instruments.
messages.2536:
Both of them had their eyes closed, lost in a world of their
own.
messages.2600:
As can be expected from sisters, their rhythm was in exact
synchronization.
messages.2660:
Mako was playing as normal as a flute can get, but
Moe-senpai's xylophone playing was somehow...
messages.2737:
It wasn't a case of being skilled or unskilled here. From
the flowing music, the whimsical mood of the two could be
felt.
messages.2844: Moe-senpai especially looked like she was...ehh?
messages.2881:
All of a sudden, Moe-senpai's music flew up in terms of
power.
messages.2930: The sudden change in tempo... amazing.
messages.3027: "Wait, onee-chan! You fell out of sync again!"
messages.3078: Mako removed her mouth from her flute to rebuke her sister.
messages.3166: With a perplexed expression, Moe's hands stopped moving.
messages.3241: "Don't just say "Eh?". You slid off there."
messages.3335:
Moe-senpai apologized deeply. Her demeanour made her seem
more like a caretaker or guardian.
messages.3395: "Aw, it was fine. I thought it was a great performance."
messages.3627: I could feel Mako's bloodthirst growing.
messages.3727:
In direct contrast, Moe-senpai's greeting was delivered with
a pleasant smile.
messages.3802: I greeted Moe-senpai, and kept a safe distance from Mako.
messages.3951: "No, I can see that, I mean..."
messages.4024:
"We're practicing the performance for the opening ceremony
in April."
messages.4071:
"Ah, the opening ceremony for high-school... not
unsurprising that the music club would perform there. You'd
be playing your flute?
messages.4153:
If nothing else, I definitely admire Mako for her musical
skills.
messages.4224:
"What would a freshman like me be doing playing there? I'm
just watching over my sister practicing."
messages.4372:
A tinge of anxiety marked her words and smile as she
answered my question.
messages.4444:
It's pretty understandable to be a bit nervous in that
situation.
messages.4509: "Well... there's still a month to practice."
messages.4656:
"Yes, thank you very much. On the day, I'd put all my heart
into welcoming you and Mako."
messages.4753:
At my words, Moe-senpai and Mako both exchanged glances and
smiles.
messages.4811: "Well then, do your best till then."
messages.4912: I go out the soundproofed door, back into the corridor.
messages.4962:
...Speaking of which, amazing that Mako's voice could pierce
through this "barrier"...
messages.5173:
I saw Moe-senpai and Mako in the music room on Sunday. They
were practicing a piece for the freshmen welcoming
reception.
messages.5263:
I felt that the performance was good, but apparently Moe's
playing was a bit rushed.
messages.5361:
On another note, I completely forgot about Suginami's
affairs earlier.

messages.249:
The first words of my last memory of her was rather
uncomplimentary.
messages.318:
--That is, whenever I think of my childhood friend
Sakuranbo, this is always the first memory that pops up.
messages.417:
The wind was strong-- the strongest of the entire Spring
season.
messages.452:
Under the Sakura tree that did not wither the year before, I
remove my hands from my ears and release a sigh.
messages.522: "...Why are you always trying to do that?"
messages.569:
It's like striking your head against a brick wall to break
it...
messages.616: Or is this her form of greeting the tree?
messages.649:
The girl, after tonight, will be moving far away. Yet she
remained glaring at the tree, angry for no discernable
reason.
messages.737: I rest my head on the metal bat on my shoulder.
messages.824: "By the way onii-chan, why are you carrying a bat around?"
messages.971: "Why not? Nemu-chan always calls you that!"
messages.1132:
"Since your birthday comes first, I should be calling you
onee-chan instead..."
messages.1208:
Looks like the number of little sisters I have is
increasing.
messages.1245:
Even if I had one dozen little sisters, I bet she'd still
insist on being one.
messages.1339:
"I don't want you calling me onee-chan... you're always the
one protecting me after all."
messages.1409:
My cousin's shoulders dropped. Her muttered words after were
inaudible to me.
messages.1489:
"Well, whatever. No matter how many times I tell you to, you
won't stop anyway."
messages.1545: "And, I brought a bat because of this."
messages.1578:
I showed her an envelope with "fight challenge" written on
it, then opened it and read it aloud.
messages.1648:
"Be at the dead sakura tree at 3 PM today. If you don't
appear, you will see your family members dead...."
messages.1757:
The definition of desperation, threatening innocents' lives.
Having understood the situation, I got there 15 minutes
early.
messages.1835:
"Since you're moving away, I suppose you wanted to have a
"final confrontation" of sorts?"
messages.1967: "From reading this, it's hard to think otherwise."
messages.2040:
"Since it's such a huge thing, I copied that from a play I
read once."
messages.2120: "And just look at how you've made things..."
messages.2180:
"How on earth did my uncle's daughter get such... words,
from a play...
messages.2429:
"Yeah. That's why... I don't know when we'd be able to meet
again, so I want you to make a promise to me."
messages.2517: "Not true. If you're lonely, I'd go and keep you company."
messages.2612: On that day, Nemu was nowhere to be found--
messages.2661: and my real reason to come here was lost.
messages.2715:
If Nemu--my little sister did not exist... maybe I would be
more comfortable with her calling me that.
messages.2841: "You can board an aeroplane by yourself?"
messages.2876: "Ehh!? Can't you reach America by train?"
messages.3076:
Her eyes started to tear up, and my heart started beating
faster.
messages.3188: It's not much different from when Nemu's parents died--
messages.3256:
My heard throbbed painfully, and I berated myself for
remembering that subject again.
messages.3372:
"That's why I want you to make a promise with me, under this
sakura tree."
messages.3522: I closed my eyes and murmured quietly.
messages.3707: As I opened my eyes, Sakuranbo still had her head down.
messages.3763: "I can still write letters and call you."
messages.3834:
"Grow up fast when you get there. If you get bullied again,
I can't save you this time."
messages.3943:
"I can't grow up so fast~... besides, they don't usually
tease me about my height..."
messages.4074:
Well, if she gets teased by guys, that usually means they
like her anyway...
messages.4304: "When I'm really in trouble, come save me..."
messages.4415:
Although she was always bullied, since I was protecting her,
she was able to hold on...
messages.4499: I honestly don't know what'd happen when I'm not there.
messages.4601: "I don't need a promise to save you. I'd do it without one."
messages.4736: Stuttering a bit, but at least smiling.
messages.4759:
I show her my hand, and after a bit of movement, make a
wagashi appear from it.
messages.4918:
Sakuranbo murmured, the only person on earth who knows about
my power.
messages.4974:
"You okay now? If you don't go, grandpa and grandma're going
to leave you behind."
messages.5123: Her voice revberberated through the falling sakura petals.
messages.5280: For once, her voice fell silent.
messages.5330: "You and me, when we meet again..."
messages.5394: A wind getting stronger and stronger.
messages.5417:
As her last words disappeared into the wind, Sakuranbo took
a deep breath and chewed on her lower lip.
messages.5574:
At the sound of a bell, and another one of a television
changing channels, everything went white.
messages.5805:
The day when we were still kids, with the words "Die!"
ringing in my ears.
messages.5860:
I found out that America could not be reached by train. The
same America that Sakura was going to...
messages.5964: So the two of us made promises...

messages.167: I had a dream about something deep in my memory.
messages.206: A dream about the day my cousin, and childhood friend, left.
messages.260:
I've had this sort of dream for two days in a row now...
what's going on?
messages.390:
I could hear the noisy chatter of the street outside, the
sunlight on my eyelids. I felt I wouldn't be able to fall
asleep again.
messages.571:
On the only day of the week which can be used for rest...
it'd be a shame not to use it.
messages.868: Sunday awaited me after waking up from a bittersweet dream.
messages.908: To get up, or to try to sleep again...

messages.111: Naah... I'd sleep a bit longer...
messages.148:
After turning onto my other side, I quickly lose
consciousness again.
messages.223: The bustle of the street gradually grew distant...
messages.428: In the end, I continue sleeping.

messages.129:
Even if I'm still tired, I'd get up. No point in letting the
long-awaited rest day pass over on top of my bed.
messages.281:
I open my eyes, and quickly become acquainted with the
ceiling.
messages.356:
I rise into a sitting position on my bed, and release a huge
yawn.
messages.418: Now then, where is that Nemu?
messages.459: I hope she's resting to heal her condition.
messages.525:
With a forceful yell, I jump up, and change into my usual
clothes.
messages.682: "You're up already? How are you feeling?"
messages.762: "I'm fine. As always, refreshed from the sleep."
messages.822:
Smiling bitterly to myself at Nemu's words, I plop onto the
sofa and start searching for the remote control.
messages.903: "Brother, I'm going to meet up with Miharu."
messages.952:
"Going out? Are you sure you'd be okay after you collapsed
yesterday?"
messages.1043:
"I told you I was feeling fine, didn't I? Besides, what
better day to have fun that a Sunday.♪"
messages.1200: Sinking my advice with that smile of hers, she heads out.
messages.1275: I slump deeper into the sofa, and sigh loudly.
messages.1335: "Don't blame me if your condition worsens again."
messages.1733:
Although she wasn't fully well yet, Nemu still went out with
Miharu.
messages.1793:
Really... I don't know if her condition really is bad or
not.

messages.135: "Waaaah... that was a good, long rest."
messages.166: I get up from my bed and stretch.
messages.251:
I energetically jump off the bed, change into some casual
clothes, and head out of my room.
messages.360: "Speaking of which, has Nemu woken up already?"
messages.399:
She's not in her room above mine, and I don't see her figure
downstairs either.
messages.490: On the table lay a small pink-coloured piece of memo paper.
messages.548: "Brother. I'm feeling fine now, so I went to meet Miharu."
messages.653:
She should be resting fully during the convalescence
period...
messages.713:
(Well, I guess I should be happy enough that she's already
recovering so quickly.)
messages.836: Putting my wallet in my pocket, I head for the door.
messages.1035:
After waking up and going to the living room, I found Nemu's
note on the table.
messages.1099:
Although her condition hasn't fully healed yet, she still
went to Miharu's. Sigh, she really doesn't care about the
convalescence period...

messages.133:
With the sun's warm rays beating down onto my body, I stroll
down the shopping district.
messages.180:
On Sundays, the shopping district is always bustling with
activity. Within that, I aimlessly walk around.
messages.272:
A nicely-decorated roadside shop only grabbed the attention
of my eyes for a second.
messages.373:
After paying a visit to a bookshop and CD shop, I return to
the strolling masses.
messages.431:
From all the boredom, I get a sudden urge to go to the park
and chase down the pidgeons there.
messages.495: "Maybe I can buy something while I'm here...?"
messages.530:
Do I need to buy anything? I searched my brain for
provisions a household needs...
messages.653:
With a hum, my brain works takes inventory control
perfectly, revealing no needed supplies.
messages.727:
"Well, maybe I should buy like 10 extra of each, for
emergency supplies."
messages.823:
Not to mention it'd be a great way to get out of provision
shopping for awhile.
messages.905:
Then again, if I do something like that, I'd have to prepare
myself for the wrath of Demon Nemu...
messages.1018: Rummage through someone else's garbage out of boredom?
messages.1091:
"...Speaking of which, maybe I should buy some chocolates to
send to Sakura?"
messages.1157:
Just window shopping is tiresome. It'd be better if I had a
goal to work towards.
messages.1262: Yeah, I won't postpone it any longer.
messages.1403:
"Choco-in-Jelly" "Buy 40 get 4 free" "Milk and Fruit & Nut
flavours available"
messages.1490:
Of course, at this period they haven't started selling White
Day chocolates yet.
messages.1552:
"(Well, at least in the off-season, the prices are
cheaper.)"
messages.1620: I picked up a huge "board" of chocolate.
messages.1729: I start looking for a more normal box of chocolates.
messages.1770:
As I put the chocolate board back on it's shelf, under it, I
see chocolates with the word "NEW" written above them.
messages.1846: "This should be good, if they're "NEW" and all."
messages.1889:
With the almond chocolate with unknown "NEW"ness in hand, I
head to the register while rummaging through my wallet.
messages.2148: For some reason, I ended up at the shopping district.
messages.2179:
I offhandedly remembered about Sakura's Valentine's gift,
and bought something to return the favour.

messages.157:
Sunday afternoon, I'm walking down a nameless street. All by
myself, just idly loitering around.
messages.233:
Then again, I certainly wouldn't mind if someone else was
walking with me.
messages.289: Such as a couple of cute girls.
messages.351:
Although spring is coming, the Feburary weather is still
stiffening to the body. People still walk around in winter
clothing. ;[name]
messages.509: Looks like it's not the time for light wear yet...
messages.546: "Someone, please knit a sweater for me right now..."
messages.597:
Thinking crazy thoughts, I enter a book and CD shop for the
warmth, and continue loafing around.
messages.772:
As I gradually leave the shop, I started thinking of other
places to go.
messages.885:
I don't feel like being in a crowd today, so going to a
movie is out of the question. To say nothing of going to a
coffeeshop.
messages.977: "I guess the safest option would be the park..."
messages.1063:
I saw from the TV once that sakura trees are in full bloom
in April, but that's a law of nature that doesn't apply
here.
messages.1188:
This park continually gets cleaned up, yet the sakura petals
continue to fall to the point where it's hard to walk
through.
messages.1272: "...And that may be why no one else is around."
messages.1311:
As I predicted, the only ones walking around the park are a
few elderly people.
messages.1403:
I'd be bored if I take the normal route through as well.
Instead, I go off the path and into the forest of sakura
trees.
messages.1491:
The smell of the sakura petals grew stronger. If I touch one
of the sakura tree's trunks now, it'd feel cold to the
touch.
messages.1614:
As I look up, the sky was hidden, covered by a thin shade of
pink.
messages.1725: Close to here is the secret base I used to have as a child.
messages.1787: Of course, if I look at it now, it wasn't much of one.
messages.1839:
But when I was a kid, and when it was bigger than my hands
outstretched, it was a very important place for me.
messages.1952:
As I murmured that, my feet started heading in the direction
of that place.
messages.2057: The sakura are in full bloom.
messages.2072:
Ever since young, I always thought of this huge sakura tree
as my second home.
messages.2138:
To others, it looks overwhelming, yet it has such a gentle
air to it.
messages.2192: "...Even if I look at it now, it's still amazing."
messages.2322: The sakura petals that cling to ones lips.
messages.2349: All these various things mirror the dreams I've often had.
messages.2455: Suddenly, nearby, I could hear someone singing.
messages.2537: Sounding like a fairy's song, I thought weirdly.
messages.2595:
While the location might be odd, the singing itself is
beautiful.
messages.2636:
It's a foreign song. While the words are incomprehensible to
me, I can at least tell that the melody is beautiful.
messages.2735:
I slowly move closer to the sound of the song-- from the
rear of the huge sakura tree.
messages.2813:
Within the dancing sakura petals, a young girl, her hair
fluttering, was singing her song.
messages.2910:
I can't think of anything to say or do, just stare and feel
the song.
messages.3136:
Like humans from the planet of the apes meeting, we stared
at each other.
messages.3200:
The singing ceased immediately. My ear still felt the
reveberations of her song.
messages.3486:
"...When I sing, I completely forget about everything around
me."
messages.3564: She giggled slightly, and poked her head.
messages.3607:
With these conditions, and given the amazing song I just
heard, I thought of making a joke.
messages.3879: "Really now, how long have you been here?"
messages.3912: "When, well, around 2-3 minutes ago or so."
messages.3972:
Although I said that, I had completely lost all sense of
time while listening to her song.
messages.4036: Well, it's probably no longer than an hour...
messages.4191:
"So, you couldn't have been here longer than 10 minutes, I
think."
messages.4251:
"Ahh, I see. You left off at a great time to notice me as
well, then."
messages.4397:
She laughed with a sweet smile, a smile filled with
tenderness. Just then, a sakura petal floated into her face.
messages.4532: "whawhawha, what was that? It happened so fast..."
messages.4581:
"The sakura petals must be delighted that you were singing
here, and were showing their appreciation."
messages.4649:
While saying that, I grabbed her hat, which slipped off her
head, and returned it to it's original position.
messages.4753: "Thank you. I only just noticed that."
messages.4848:
It's not exactly easy to predict the falling patterns of a
falling sakura petal anyway...
messages.4926: It'd be simpler to think that it just wanted to fall there.
messages.5116: "Ah, never mind. What were we saying?"
messages.5151: Oy, what's with these weird conversation bits?
messages.5213:
It's like trying to catch a tennis ball with a baseball
glove; that's how I felt trying to catch what she was saying
at times.
messages.5293: "Anyway, any chance that you remember me?"
messages.5332: But for a first meeting for her, it couldn't really happen.
messages.5432:
The surprise on her face made me feel slightly disappointed.
Am I such an easily forgettable person?
messages.5506:
I start to remember the first conversation I had with the
person in front of me.
messages.5574: ...And I suppose there was nothing "slightly" about it.
messages.5788: I ended up in the Sakura Park.
messages.5853: I met up with Kotori there. She was singing a song.
messages.5909: However, I got a shock when she couldn't remember me.

messages.125: It was the day of last year's Christmas party.
messages.162: I was sleeping in the corner of the PE storehouse.
messages.247:
I had a weird feeling that someone else was around. I looked
up, and in my field of vision was...
messages.334:
Long hair with the moonlight brilliantly reflecting off it,
as if the person standing there had materialized from
another world.
messages.433:
It was a person that everyone in Kazami Academy knew of. The
school idol.
messages.629:
"Oh, I'm sorry, I couldn't see you... what would you be
doing here?"
messages.707:
"Just thinking to myself... if you want, I can move. I bet
your reason for being here is at least different in the
"myself" part."
messages.826: "? ....Ah, haha. You must be a good person."
messages.930:
"Nooo, I can feel it. You're like a bubble that never
bursts."
messages.1052:
"When most bubbles reach high places, they tend to burst...
unlike you right now, I guess?"
messages.1144: "...I have no clue what you're talking about."
messages.1205:
"Hehehe. I don't really understand my own explanation
either."
messages.1269: She giggled for a bit, nodding her head slightly.
messages.1302:
She certainly didn't have the airs of a typical girl. I
start wondering whether she really is the school idol.
messages.1394:
"Well, moving the subject away from me for a second... don't
you have to go to the contest, Shirakawa?"
messages.1479:
"Yeah. It's going to start soon... but until it does, do you
mind if I stay here?"
messages.1567: "W, well... it's not my storehouse anyway."
messages.1642:
"Alright, thank you. And you don't have to call me by my
surname, Kotori is fine."
messages.2116:
The girl, who certainly didn't seem like a school idol,
stopped talking after my weird reply.
messages.2221:
At the climax of the contest when the votes were to be cast,
Nemu called me on my cellphone, wanting me to vote for her.
messages.2330:
She tried to use her reverse-mode style to try and convince
me, but I lied a bit, and said that I hated polls and
voting.
messages.2443:
It was more like, that I may not really have wanted her to
win...
messages.2684:
I remembered the time where I first met and talked to
Kotori.
messages.2750:
...It was a pretty dynsfunctional conversation, now that I
think about it.

messages.149:
After lapsing into memory-land for awhile, I snap back to
reality and looked at Kotori.
messages.331:
Before I could finish my sentence, Kotori clapped her hands
together.
messages.523: Kotori gave a thumbs-up.
messages.590: "But, why were you so reluctant to tell me your name then?"
messages.656: "I fell into a memory lapse for an hour."
messages.775: I guess... she didn't get the joke?
messages.833:
"Maaan... does this mean you won't tell me your name now
either?"
messages.958: Well, no point in hiding it now.
messages.1077: Once again, her thumb went up.
messages.1137: Mimicking her, I gave her a thumbs up as well.
messages.1176: "It's okay if I just call you Kotori, right?"

Meanwhile, after graduation, I idly let time pass through

But as I thought this, I could see the entrance of the

It definitely isn't a cat or a dog. In fact, it looks more

It's eyes look just like the kind one would find in a "How

Since whatever crashed into me screamed, I guess it was

I look around, and see a pair of glasses lying not too far

I pick up the glasses, which have a very chic and

The girl put on her glasses, and finally got a proper look
at me.

And it's all that goat's fault anyway. If it wasn't there,

"Page 13, please forgive meee! I hope you're in a better

messages.352:
If anything, she'd more likely be found there than in the
classrooms...
messages.467:
No one was here in this dark and gloomy place. Not
Tsukishiro, not anyone.
messages.545: "I'm just being stupid. I should head back..."
messages.578: I can't just solve weird problems that easily.
messages.646:
The plant was still growing there, but if yesterday hadn't
taken place, I wouldn't have been able to distinguish it.
messages.767:
Turning my back on the plant, I started heading back to
class.
messages.872: Tsukishiro had been standing behind me.
messages.909:
Her presence wasn't even noticable; how long had she been
standing there?
messages.1032:
Thinking for a while, she eventually took off her gloves,
and patted her doll.
messages.1169: "H, hello... uh, this is Tsukishiro speaking, right?"
messages.1278:
Tsukishiro calmly shook her head no, her twin curled
ponytails swinging side-to-side with her head.
messages.1386: "Therefore, the one speaking must be me, Piros."
messages.1444:
"There's no such thing as a doll, albeit one with a name,
speaking on it's own. It's ventriloquism, no? You're really
skilled."
messages.1567:
Tsukishiro's head turned upwards, staring at me. Her mouth
curled into a frown, her eyes still unwavering.
messages.1732:
"...Alright, alright, I get it. That doll is talking. That's
what's going on."
messages.1835:
Somehow, Tsukishiro... I mean, the doll, insisted that it
was the one talking.
messages.1907:
Strange as it may be (although par for the course), whether
it's the doll talking or Tsukishiro talking doesn't really
matter.
messages.2014:
Considering things that have happened, and are happening
right now, that's not anything to be surprised about.
messages.2082:
At a time like this, all you really need to do is nod and
smile.
messages.2159: "My name's not "doll"! It's Piros. Alice's only friend."
messages.2270: He's a pretty big loudmouth for a doll.
messages.2311:
"Anyway, Tsukishiro. Did you get back your student
notebook?"
messages.2418:
Alice's answer was barely audible, her head nodding slightly
once at the same time.
messages.2465:
She hasn't really had a reason to talk so far, but I get the
feeling that she's probably not very good at it to start
with.
messages.2587:
"She recieved it from Seiba-san as soon as we returned
home."
messages.2659:
The doll in Alice's arms, unchangingly expressionless,
answered for her. Somehow, he seems rather... unsubtle.
messages.2760: "...Being explained to by a doll is still a weird feeling."
messages.2828:
I'm not in their rhythm at all. The relationship between
Tsukishiro and that doll was still a mess of confusion to
me.
messages.2920:
Trying to distract myself, I idly stared at the water can at
my feet.
messages.2959: "Still taking care of that plant today?"
messages.3073:
"It's a very important flower, so of course we'd have to
take care of it extremely well."
messages.3139: Piros elaborated further on Alice's terseness.
messages.3176: "Not saying you shouldn't. But is this really a flower?"
messages.3236:
Even if it wasn't stepped on or whatever, it seems so weak,
that a strong gust of wind could probably blow it into the
air.
messages.3362: Refitting her gloves, Tsukishiro picked up the watering can.
messages.3407:
Repeating yesterday's routine, she calmly strode over to the
plant, and started to water it.
messages.3526:
For a split second, Tsukishiro had turned her head to me and
opened her mouth slightly. But before a word could escape
her lips, her concentration went back to the plant and
watering can.
messages.3649: I called out the doll's name.
messages.3678:
Yet all the doll did was sit in Tsukishiro's arms quietly,
wearing a never-fading smirk.
messages.3818:
It must be ventriloquism. It said so much that it could talk
by itself, yet now, it seemed dead as a doornail.
messages.3925:
Tsukishiro then stood up, having finished watering the
plant.
messages.4035:
With the watering can in one hand and the doll in the other,
she hurried back to the school building.
messages.4187:
I kicked the ground in a mixture of confusion and
frustration, creating a cloud of dust.
messages.4228: "...The hell is up with that girl?"
messages.4298:
But, even as incomprehensible as it is, I can't help but be
intrigued by it.
messages.4362:
Especially of that Piros, whether it's controlled by
ventriloquism or whether he's what he claims he is.
messages.4457: My eyes traveled over to the Tsukishiro's adopted plant.
messages.4498:
The faint rays of the sun were reflecting off the residue
drops of water, making the plant look as if it was shining.
messages.4625:
I thought, as I finally started digging into my lunch of
Hiroshima pastry cakes.
messages.4867:
Thinking about Tsukishiro, I visited the gym rear and met
her again.
messages.4941:
As before, she let the doll do the talking for her. I asked
her a lot of questions, but she remained just as
tight-lipped as yesterday.
messages.5080:
Looking at the flower she was raising, I knew one thing for
sure; she'd keep coming back here.

messages.200:
I thought that as I exited the school premises, and found
two familiar faces.

"Nope, we just thought we should eat something different

messages.540: Suginami expressed my own thoughts clear as day.
messages.581: Are we having a good synchro rate? I'm going to be sick.
messages.693: "Er... I was thinking the same thing."
messages.762:
"Ohhh, indeed, indeed! Our minds are one. Indeed, our
burning friendship binds us together!"
messages.850: I waved my hand dismissively at Suginami.
messages.885:
Whether or not I accepted it though, I really was thinking
that.
messages.960:
"Then, let the three of us experience the most wonderous of
lunchtimes!"
messages.1060: "Uh, you mean eating at a restaurant?"
messages.1133:
"Mm. You said you knew a good Japanese-style restaurant,
Kudou. Elaborate!"
messages.1253:
"If we go outside to eat now, we definitely won't make it
back for afternoon classes."
messages.1354:
As Kudou's serious face lightly admonished Suginami, I
nodded sagely at his side.
messages.1473: And what would Nemu say if she found out.
messages.1512: "Let's just go to a convenience store."
messages.1616: "...Yeah, that kind of change is acceptable."
messages.1712:
Then, the three of us walked to a nearby convenience and
provisions store.
messages.1790:
Just buying things isn't amazingly interesting, but doing it
with friends always makes it more enjoyable.
messages.2075:
Wanting a change from the usual lunchtime menu, I went with
Suginami and Kudou to a nearby convenience store to buy some
take-out.

messages.133:
The class was bubbling with excitement today. Apparently
there was another transfer student in the neighbouring
class.
messages.228:
Apparently, it's a girl, and she has some strange reasons
for transferring here, from what I heard chattering around
my desk.
messages.335:
I can't really believe that this transfer student would
transfer to a different school out of an unrequited love...
messages.463:
With Koyomi-sensei's entrance into the classroom, the bustle
of the classroom died quickly as the attendance was marked.
messages.564:
"This week is examination week, so make sure you study hard
for it."
messages.652:
Koyomi-sensei's "words of encouragement" certainly didn't
sound like them.
messages.704: More like a threat to the students.
messages.725:
Koyomi-sensei went through the usual things, and then ended
homeroom.
messages.962:
Today, a transfer student came into the other class, and
caused some excitement in this one.
messages.1034:
The transfer student's dramatic love... sounds more like a
kid's dream, and the subject was quickly changed to worrying
about the coming exams.

messages.127:
The scratching of chalk on blackboard was closely mirrored
by the scribbling of pen on note paper.
messages.241:
Just as I realized I had miswritten an earlier passage of
text, it was erased from the blackboard.
messages.370:
At the very front of the class, right in front of the
teacher's desk, Nemu had her head down, furiously copying
notes.
messages.460: I can just copy them from Nemu later, I suppose.
messages.664:
I didn't manage to write down a passage from the blackboard
before it was erased. But it's still okay. Nemu's in this
class.
messages.761:
While Nemu's around, there's no need to worry about taking
notes.

messages.178: "And that ends the class. Weekly duty, rise."
messages.254: After calling out attendance, Koyomi bade us farewell.
messages.329: I make a small guts pose under my desk.
messages.370: She ended the class 5 minutes earlier than usual.
messages.458:
I bow with respect and affection for Koyomi-sensei, while my
lower half was tingling... meaning my leg, really.
messages.555:
"(Although at this rate, during lunch period, I'm almost
certainly going to get entangled into Sakura again...)"
messages.629:
--The sight of her face in my mind's eye made me stop in my
tracks.
messages.823: Holding her purse, Nemu walked past my side.
messages.883: "That's odd... did you forget your lunchbox?"
messages.924:
Unlike myself who eats at the cafeteria nearly every day,

messages.1059: "Noo... I just felt like eating at the cafeteria today."
messages.1115: She talked to me with a slightly sulky voice.
messages.1225: "Sigh... because of the girl with puberty problems."

messages.1358:
I didn't really understand what Nemu meant, but decided not
to think too much about it.
messages.1491:
As I turn around, Mako's face is the first thing in my
vision.
messages.1630:
"Nothing. Just trying to perfect a scowl to neutralize your
punch."
messages.1744:
"...Still being stupid. Onee-chan is waiting for me, I'm
going now."
messages.1827: With a wave of my hand, I see her back off.
messages.1910:
Opening the door to the corridor, I decided on my lunchtime
spot.
messages.2115:
Class ended 5 minutes earlier than normal. I cheered and did
a small guts pose.

messages.180: I carried some yakisoba bread and croquette bread with me.

item.

I find a good bench with some sun shining onto it, and

"That's really a lot, Asakura-kun. You must've spent a lot

"It'd be worth it. I won't get fat on it or anything

messages.917:
I probably should've said something helpful then, but I

messages.1104:
An exact figure for a cloudy subject... where'd the whole

With her acceptance and smile, I take the yakisoba bread out

"Well, as long as it tastes good, how it looks shouldn't

"Yup, it was a battle of epic proportions to acquire this

messages.2364: I ate lunch with Kotori in the courtyard.

"Now that I think about it, this is an indirect kiss isn't

The lunchbox showed obvious care in catering to all the

We started our lunch in peace, in the deserted school

But once I handed over the bread and she took a bite, the

The embarassed Kotori then quickly finished the whole bread
before the possibility could become the truth.

Mumbling something, she took a bite from the side opposite

messages.1789: She handed me her lunchbox with a sweet smile.

messages.1944: "Ohh. In that case, you can have this one too."

The lunchbox showed obvious care in catering to all the

We started our lunch in peace, in the deserted school

But once I handed over the bread ahd she took a bite, the

The embarassed Kotori then quickly finished the whole bread

messages.141: Time to secure today's afternoon rations.

messages.230:
But the competition is fierce... it might be sold out by now
already.

messages.562: "It isn't quite something I wear at all times."

messages.759: "That costume is only for special circumstances..."

messages.897: Well, if she wants to keep it private, I can't say anything.

messages.985:
"If you were hanging around here, I guess you had to buy
lunch today?"
messages.1079:
"Yes. As I had forgotten my lunchbox today, I thought that
if I didn't hurry, there would be nothing left."
messages.1267:
Tamaki held in her hands, the prized possession that men
would come to blows for; yakisoba bread.
messages.1378: Praying for a positive response, I enquired.
messages.1413: Tamaki's expression turned to one of ponderance.
messages.1476: "I don't believe so... the one I have, was the last."
messages.1656:
"Well... at the time I left, there was a sudden flood for
bread at the store, so..."
messages.1821: Looks like I'd have to skip lunch today.
messages.1966: Seeing my crestfallen state, Tamaki started to speak.
messages.2015:
"Yeah, there aren't many in stock every day. On top of that,
it's delicious, so there's always a scramble for them."
messages.2109:
Even with the luck of the devil himself, you'd be
hard-pressed to eat it more than once a week.
messages.2211: "And, you like this type of bread?"
messages.2373:
Tamaki's envisage transformed to that of an angel,
descending from the cloudy sky.
messages.2439:
Or if not that, a spider hanging from it's web in the depths
of hell.
messages.2519: But, if I take this, what about Tamaki?
messages.2633: "It's fine. I still have a packet of melon bread, as well."
messages.2701: She showed me her other packet, smiling.
messages.2753: Those actions and movements... how cute.
messages.2874: Today, I am a dog with it's tail up.
messages.2923: People may say things about it being an unfair trade,
messages.2972: But I have no ears for them today.
messages.3019:
The words I heard immediately after, didn't tally too well
with my stance.
messages.3151:
As soon as she handed the yakisoba bread to me, she quickly
returned to the classroom.
messages.3249: "(You don't have to go so fast...)"
messages.3294:
After all that, I was going to ask to eat together, but I
couldn't call her out before she left.
messages.3397:
Well, for better or for worse... there's no doubt that she's

messages.3729:
She was coming back from buying bread herself. According to
her, it's probably all sold out by now.
messages.3805:
Seeing my crestfallen state, Tamaki insisted on giving me
part of hers, no strings attached.
messages.3897: She's a little weird, but she's definitely a kind person.

messages.153:
There was no real reason to go there, but in the end, I
thought it was a good idea to check on it's condition.
messages.239: I wasn't looking to create trouble or anything.
messages.284:
But since Miharu wasn't around, and we'd actually met, I
wanted to try to get closer to her.
messages.374: Of course, I was talking about Tsukishiro Alice.
messages.409:
Thinking that maybe she may not be here at this time, I
furtively approached the spot.
messages.471:
But, as my view became clearer and clearer, so did the
figure of Tsukishiro.
messages.572: The tiny Tsukishiro snapped her head towards me.
messages.689:
"I can understand it needing water during lunch break at
noon, but what are you doing here after school?"
messages.767:
Squirming, she once again removed her gloves and brought the
doll's head to face me.
messages.842:
Her innocence and purity were reflected in her eyes, as she
gazed at me.
messages.867: She didn't look comfortable at all.
messages.911:
"If we don't watch out here after school, that old janitor
will come around and rip the plant out!"
messages.997:
"...So, you're gonna stay there the whole time, doing
nothing but staring at it?"
messages.1087:
"We don't know when or whether that old guy will come!! We
can't just let it happen."
messages.1165:
"...Tell him when he comes, then leave. You can't stay here
forever."
messages.1318: Her eyes continued piercing into my very soul.
messages.1363: Looks like she hasn't noticed it at all.
messages.1400:
The said part-time janitor was already walking around,
pulling out the weeds around the campus.
messages.1575: I ran up to the janitor, and started explaining.
messages.1649: "He understands not to tear that plant out now."
messages.1733: "...I thought I was supposed to go talk to him."
messages.1774:
"Uh, you mean, letting this doll talk to him? He'd run off
screaming in terror first."
messages.1856:
Not that I'm calling myself Mr. Congeniality, but I'm at
least human.
messages.2025:
"Anyway, it should be alright even if you don't stare at it
24-7 now."
messages.2091:
In this deserted area, only that janitor would think of
encroaching this restricted space anyway.
messages.2236:
"We don't know what might happen... we'd continue keeping
watch for a bit longer."
messages.2300:
As both Tsukishiro and Piros finished talking, they went
back to boring holes into the plant with their eyes.
messages.2386: Seems like no one can stop them.
messages.2431:
Tsukishiro continued squatting next to the plant, showing no
signs of movement at all.
messages.2468:
If it wasn't for her occasional blinking, you'd think that
what she was carrying wasn't the only doll around.
messages.2577:
"Are you really going to keep watching over it? It's going
to get dark soon, you know?"
messages.2639:
Coldness had started to creep in the air, and the sun was
starting to fall behind the clouds; it was time to head
back.
messages.2752: "Our houses are close, why don't we go home together?"
messages.2801: I'm starting to get the shivers, sheesh!
messages.2863: Her skin even looks as white as snow...
messages.2906:
That tiny body can't possibly stand up so long to the
freezing winds of the end of Feburary...
messages.3058:
She suddenly stood up, taking the bag beside her, and ran
off.
messages.3169: By the time I noticed, she'd all but disappeared.
messages.3211:
I tried to chase after her, but the speed at which she ran
made her uncatchable.
messages.3293: She's far more agile than I tbought.
messages.3320: Her figure raced into the Sakura Park opposite the gym,
messages.3414: but by the time I reached there, she had vanished.
messages.3525:
Slowing down to catch my breath, the surroundings were
completely silent besides my panting.
messages.3597: "Oh well, I'd buy a chocolate banana and head back."
messages.3646: Better head home before I catch a cold.
messages.3851:
Visting the gym rear, I found Tsukishiro staring intently at
the flower there.
messages.3923:
Apparently, she was afraid some passerby would rip it out,
thinking it was a weed.
messages.4001:
In Tsukishiro's stead, I explained to the janitor to ignore
the plant at the back of the gym.
messages.4071:
Then, I invited Tsukishiro to head back to our homes
together, but she more or less refused...

messages.149:
As I wandered aimlessly around the shopping district, I felt
a knock on my shoulder.
messages.248: "Yo, Asakura. You look free."
messages.279:
"Not really... I actually have a painfully detailed schedule
of which places I loiter at, by the minute."
messages.456: Right after Suginami came Kudou, smiling wryly.
messages.531:
"Asakura, how about a game of air hockey? We haven't played
that in a long time."

messages.709: "Hmm, another "how troublesome" from you, I bet?"
messages.752:
Suginami grinned widely at me. His words somehow vexed me,
and I decided to take up his offer.
messages.919:
"Mm, now that's more like a man! Kudou, you're a fair

Being appointed as judge rather abruptly, Kudou looked at us
in surprise.
messages.1138:
"Yeah, since you're a common friend, we can expect complete

messages.1250:
"Even so... it's just a game, why are you two so serious
about it?"
messages.1344:
Tsk tsk tsk, Suginami and I waved our fingers at Kudou in

messages.1438:
"You don't understand. A true man treats everything he does
seriously!"
messages.1612:
"Haah... one time cool as ice, another hot-blooded. I'd

messages.1692:
He released a long sigh as we dragged him to the game
center.
messages.1960: Suginami challenged me to a battle of air hockey.

Once that was decided, we dragged Kudou along with us to the

messages.129:
"(Why do I always feel like sleeping during the afternoon
classes...)"

Of course, knowing the feelings of some book's character

messages.329:
This class would be more centered on trying to increase our
capability of reading and understanding literature...
messages.606: I "sleepstudy" my way through the literature class.

messages.325:
Encountering a crazy goat, being bumped into by Nanako and
getting her important things devoured...
messages.360: This'd never have happened if that stupid goat didn't exist.
messages.430:
I suddenly recalled a copy of "Nuu" that I borrowed form
Suginami awhile ago...
messages.498:
It had a special feature on white and black magic, and the
symbol representing evilness, was a goat.
messages.607:
I couldn't help comparing the likeness of the two images
before my eyes...
messages.675: A cold shiver ran down my spine.
messages.718: "Grr... I should look into ways to exorcise it."
messages.765:
My feet headed to the direction of the only shrine on this
island.
messages.858:
The busiest period of shinto shrines is obviously the new
year.
messages.905:
But even besides that, even a small shrine like this usually
gets quite a few worshippers.
messages.971: It was odd to see only one other person around, like now.
messages.1152: Her face was questioning why I was here, just like my own.
messages.1311:
Taking a closer look, she was holding it close to her chest,
indeed.
messages.1375: I can't read what was written on it.
messages.1414:
Well, I'm not the kind to sneakily invade other people's
privacy, but...
messages.1474:
"Votive picture...? You mean the kind you make a wish on?
What kind of wish did you make?"
messages.1619:
"Wahhh! D, don't look! I, if other people see the wish, it
